description: How real BLE Live receivers deviate from the PDF, and what a sensor designer must do about it. Dates are when the behaviour was verified against receiver source or on the bench.

quirks.summary: Numbers equipment types from 0 while the spec's Table 10 starts at 1. Only 21 (Activity Monitor) and 120 (Heart Rate Monitor) agree.
quirks.rule: Say which numbering your receivers use before choosing an Equipment Type value; test with the receiver, not the table.

quirks.summary: WASP keys on Equipment Type 11 as the ANT+ bike power device type and forwards each BLE Live power frame as ANT+ page 0x10. The spec's Table 10 gives 11 to Running Speed. The WYMU live flavor sends 11.
quirks.rule: A power sensor meant for WASP sends 11. Treat 11 as ambiguous when decoding unknown devices.

quirks.summary: If a DFD's first field byte is 0x01, 0x03, 0x07, 0x0F, 0x1F, 0x3F, 0x4F or 0xFF and its popcount equals the number of bytes after it, GatewayKit treats that byte as a flag and drops it.
quirks.rule: Never start a DFD with such an index when the count matches, e.g. Model # (0x03) followed by two fields. The WYMU lists Firmware Version (5) first for this reason.

quirks.summary: Hardware Version (meta 4) is Uint8 in Table 6 and in the WASP .NET code, but GatewayKit reads two bytes and the spec's own Appendix B example encodes two bytes.
quirks.rule: Leave Hardware Version out until the spec settles the width.

quirks.summary: CoreBluetooth exposes only Apple's fixed advertisementData keys; AD types 0xFE and 0xFD never reach app code. Android (ScanRecord.getBytes) and gateways do see them.
quirks.rule: iOS apps cannot receive BLE Live directly; route through a WASP/GEM gateway or a connection.

quirks.receiver: WASP/GEM radios in passive scan mode, DFU Helper
quirks.summary: A passive scanner never sees the scan response. The reference design puts the live structure in the scan response; the WYMU moved it to the primary advert (flags + manufacturer data + live frame) and the name to the scan response.
quirks.rule: Put the BLE Live structure in the primary advertising packet and budget 31 bytes around it. Apps that identify the device by name must use manufacturer data instead.

quirks.receiver: GatewayKit NPEBLELiveData.m, WASP .NET, this reference design
quirks.summary: Key = SHA-256(private key 16 B || device id 4 B LE)[0:16]; AES-128-CTR with counter block = fixed nonce 01..0C || 4-byte counter; the counter is sent little-endian after the device id; no MAC. None of this is in the spec text.
quirks.rule: Implement exactly this or nothing decrypts; expect the spec to document it in a later revision.

quirks.summary: The DPI may be truncated after the last non-zero byte (spec 1.1). The WYMU sends FF 01 03.
quirks.rule: Decoders must accept 1 to 8 DPI bytes.

quirks.summary: Stores the first DFD it sees for each index and never updates it, and silently drops a DFV whose DFD it has not seen.
quirks.rule: A device must not change a DFD's field list while running; a receiver that missed the DFD shows nothing until restarted, so send DFDs often (fast phase and every 4 s).

quirks.summary: Has no handling for the DPI (0xFF); it learns packets from DFDs alone.
quirks.rule: Do not rely on the DPI for discovery; the DFDs must be complete on their own.

quirks.summary: Its meta table has 14 = Zone Thresholds (byte array) and 15 = UI Characteristics, while spec 1.5.1+ has 14 = Zone Threshold Size and 15 = Zone Thresholds. Indexes 0-13 and the fitness table agree with the spec (Hardware Version is one byte there).
quirks.rule: Avoid meta indexes 14 and 15 until the library and the spec agree.

quirks.summary: nRF5 SDK's ble_advdata has no AD type 0xFE/0xFD; the reference design patches ble_advdata.c/.h with ble_advdata_live_data_t and p_live_broadcast_data.
quirks.rule: On another SDK, append the raw structure yourself: length, 0xFE, device id LE, DI, payload.

quirks.summary: To see raw 0xFE/0xFD frames: a GEM3 PoE forwards raw adverts in its multicast stream; nRF Connect for Mobile on Android shows 'Unknown EIR (0xFE): <hex>'. macOS cannot (CoreBluetooth), and passive helpers miss scan responses.
quirks.rule: Capture with Android nRF Connect or a GEM3; paste the hex into decode_capture.
